contests.title: Proposition 423: Vail Unified School District budget override continuation
contests.scopeNote: Voters of Vail Unified School District No. 20.

measures.questionText:
Shall the Governing Board of Vail Unified School District No. 20 of Pima County, Arizona (the “School
District”), adopt maintenance and operations budgets which allow the School District to continue to
exceed the revenue control limit specified by law in the amount of not more than twelve and one-
half percent (12.5%) per fiscal year for fiscal year 2027/2028 and the next subsequent six (6) fiscal years
thereafter?

The 2027/2028 proposed continuation of the budget increase of the School District budget will
exceed the alternate proposed School District budget by approximately $5,102,762. The amount of the
proposed increase will be based on a percentage of the School District’s revenue control limit in future
years as provided in Section 15-481(P), Arizona Revised Statutes. Any budget increase continuation
authorized by this election shall be entirely funded by a levy of taxes on the taxable property in this
School District for the year for which adopted and for six subsequent years, shall not be realized from
monies furnished by the state and shall not be subject to the limitation on taxes specified in article IX,
section 18, Constitution of Arizona. Based on the current net assessed valuation used for secondary
property tax purposes, to fund the proposed continuation of the increase in the School District’s budget
would require an estimated continuation of a tax rate of $1.61 per $100 of assessed valuation used for
secondary property tax purposes and is in addition to the School District’s tax rate that will be levied to
fund the School District’s revenue control limit allowed by law.

voterGuide.summary:
VAIL UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT NO. 20
NOVEMBER 3, 2026

SPECIAL OVERRIDE ELECTION

On June 2, 2026, the Governing Board of the District (the “Governing Board”) passed
and adopted a resolution calling a special override election (the “Election”) to authorize
the Override. A copy of such resolution is available from the District by written request
to the Superintendent, Vail Unified School District No. 20 of Pima County, Arizona,
13801 East Benson Highway #B, Vail, Arizona 85641, Telephone (520) 879-2000.
The proposed continuation of the override in the budget of the District that exceeds
the amount allowed pursuant to Section 15-905, Arizona Revised Statutes, will be not
to exceed the otherwise allowable revenue control limit by more than twelve and one-
half percent.
The proposed twelve and one-half percent override authorization is a continuation of
the District’s current twelve and one-half percent override authorization approved by
the voters in the District on November 2, 2021. The District’s current twelve and one-
half percent override authorization is required by law to be reduced by one-third in
each of fiscal years 2027/28 and 2028/29.
The total amount of the current year’s budget, the total amount of the proposed budget
and the total amount of the alternate budget are as follows:
Current Year’s Maintenance and Operations
Budget (2026/2027)				                  $146,622,048
Proposed Maintenance and Operations
Budget (2027/2028)				                  $149,717,340
Alternate Maintenance and Operations
Budget (2027/2028)				                  $144,614,578
The proposed continuation of the override in the budget would be in effect for seven
years and would allow the revenue control limit to be exceeded by not more than
twelve and one-half percent.
The proposed total amount of revenues that will fund the continuation of the override
in the budget and the amount that will be obtained from a levy of taxes on the taxable
property within the District for the first year for which the budget increase was adopted
is $15,308,286.
None of the proposed amount of revenues that will fund the continuation of the
override in the budget will be obtained from other than a levy of taxes on the taxable
property within the District.
The dollar amount for the first year for which the budget continuation was adopted is
$15,308,286, and the purpose for which the proposed continuation of the increase in
the budget is to be expended for the first year for which the budget continuation was
adopted are as follows:
• Maintain approximately 173 teaching positions paid for by the existing budget
override authority
• Provide dedicated specialty and elective area classes such as art, music, PE and
STEM
• Continue funding programs that promote high academic performance, including
programs for advanced students
• Reduce class size
• Provide additional staff to address the social, behavioral, and emotional learning
needs of students

The alternate budget shall be adopted by the Governing Board of the District if the
proposed budget is not adopted by the qualified electors of the District. In adopting
such alternate budget, the Governing Board shall follow the procedures prescribed in
Section 15-905, Arizona Revised Statutes, for adopting a budget that does not include
the proposed increase.
Please note: State statute requires that the District’s estimated fiscal year 2027/28
maintenance and operations override tax rate (shown as $1.61 per $100 of net limited
assessed property value throughout this pamphlet) be calculated using the District’s
fiscal year 2026/27 net limited assessed property value. Based on preliminary property
values provided by Pima County, it is expected that the District’s fiscal year 2027/28
net limited assessed property value will be higher than the District’s fiscal year 2026/27
net limited assessed property value, resulting in a lower 2027/28 maintenance and
operations override tax rate for the District than that presented in this pamphlet. The
District estimates that the actual fiscal year 2027/28 maintenance and operations
override tax rate will be approximately $1.55 per $100 of net limited assessed property
value, though such amount is subject to change based on final 2027/28 property values.

voterGuide.passageThreshold: A. If a proposed budget of a school district exceeds the aggregate budget limit for the budget year, at least ninety days before the proposed election the governing board shall order an override election to be held on the first Tuesday following the first Monday in November as prescribed by section 16-204, subsection F for the purpose of presenting the proposed budget to the qualified electors of the school district who by a majority of those voting either shall affirm or reject the budget.
argumentsFor:
Since 1993, generations of Vail’s children have benefited from our community’s willingness to
invest in high quality additional programs like fine arts, P.E., advanced courses, gifted services,
and lower class sizes. As a result, children have thrived, and VUSD is consistently rated a top
performing school district in Arizona.
The Vail community has benefited as well. The attractiveness of our community and the values
of our homes has been enhanced.
Please vote YES so that this generation of Vail children is assured of those same opportunities
as previous generations. Vote YES to keep our home values high and our community an
attractive place for families to live.
A “yes” vote will not increase the current tax rate because it is a continuation of an override
that is already in place.
If the override isn’t reauthorized, funding for more than 172 teaching positions will be lost.
Class sizes will increase. Valuable programs including fine arts, P.E., advanced courses, and
gifted services will be reduced.
If the override is successful, funding for those teaching positions and important programs will
be protected.
Please vote to continue support for Vail’s children. Vote YES to continue this override.
Thank you!
VUSD Governing Board

The Greater Vail Area Chamber of Commerce proudly supports Proposition 423, the Vail
Unified School District’s request to reauthorize its existing Maintenance and Operations
Budget Override.
A strong public education system is one of the foundations of a thriving community. Quality
schools help prepare the future workforce, attract families and businesses, strengthen property
values, and contribute to the long-term economic vitality of the Greater Vail area.
As our community continues to grow, maintaining the quality of Vail schools is increasingly
important. Proposition 423 is a continuation of the district’s current override, allowing Vail
Unified School District to maintain important educational programs, attract and retain
exceptional teachers and staff, and continue providing students with the high-quality
educational opportunities our community has come to expect.
Our local businesses benefit when students graduate with the skills, knowledge, and
experiences needed to succeed in college, careers, and the workforce. Investing in education
is an investment in the future of our community and local economy. Allowing this existing
funding to phase out would put teachers and programs at risk and weaken one of our
community’s greatest strengths.
For these reasons, the Greater Vail Area Chamber of Commerce encourages voters to support
Proposition 423.
Dr. Denise Bowls
President & CEO, Greater Vail Chamber of Commerce
Vail, AZ

My name is JV Nyman and am the proud parent of two Mica Mountain High School students.
I am writing in support of the upcoming override, Prop 423.
VUSD is a top-performing district, year after year, with less per-pupil funding than the state
average ($8,023 vs. $11,297). Even with the override passing, per-student funding will still fall
far below.
This override will not raise taxes. It simply continues what is already in place, replacing an
expiring override. VUSD voters have approved overrides since the 1990’s to fund the programs
that make our kids want to go to school, and keep class sizes low enough that they get the
support they need.
My family supports this override to maintain a high-quality education for our kids, keep the
community strong, and known across Arizona for its excellent schools.
Vote YES on Prop 423!
JV Nyman
Parent
Vail, AZ

I am writing to encourage registered voters residing in the Vail School District to vote for a
renewal of an override election for the Vail School District.
My husband Howard and I moved to rural Vail 56 years ago. There was one school and 350
high school students bussed to TUSD or Benson high schools. Today there are 15,000 students
attending PreK to 12th grades in attendance at 29 schools in Vail.
The override must be reauthorized by voters every five years or the funding fades away. The
money from the override is used to hire art, music, and physical education teachers as well as
specialized teachers in achievement, gifted, and advanced placement. Additional classroom
teachers are hired with the funds to assist in maintaining smaller classroom size.
The override funding is one of the reasons the Vail School District has been ranked as a top
performing district past 20 years in the State of Arizona.
The continuation of these funds is necessary to continue the award-winning educational
experiences received by each Vail student. Your “yes” vote will make sure Vail’s exceptional
educational experiences continue.
Whittley Anne Gibson
Vail School District Governing Board 2000-2012
Vail, AZ

I have lived in the Vail School District for the last 17 years and retired for the last 15 years.
This Prop is a continuation of a current Prop so this is not a new tax. I recognize that my home
value is a result of the success of the school district.
I have 3 grandchildren who have attended and graduated from schools in the Vail School
District. Over the last 15 years I have volunteered in many areas of the Vail School District and
worked as a Volunteer Coordinator and in the Counseling department in the high school. I
have also had the pleasure of being on the Governing Board from 2016 through 2020.
I have seen firsthand how the District manages the resources they have been given. This
District understands the value of the Fine Arts and extracurricular activity as an integral part to
learning. When I was a child, MANY years ago, I am sure there were grandpas who voted yes
on school overrides which impacted me directly.

It is now my opportunity to pay it forward for the children in the Vail School District. A very
wise investment. We need to continue to reward success.
Mark Tate
Vail, AZ

As a 24 year resident and mom of three in the VSD, I have watched our community grow into
a destination for families because of our commitment to educational excellence. People move
here for our top A-rated schools, and that reputation is one of our greatest assets.
Some argue that state requirements will protect our fine arts, extracurricular programs, and
specialized teachers regardless of this vote, but that is very misleading. While state standards
require arts exposure, there is a huge difference between having dedicated, certified fine arts
teachers and simply checking a legal box. If funding for specialized programs & teachers
disappears, those responsibilities fall on classroom teachers already carrying rigorous
academic demands. Voting no may result in cutting well over 100 teachers, making retention
harder and class sizes larger.
More importantly, losing fine arts specialists directly harms our children. These programs
aren’t just “checking a box.” They provide a needed mental break, foster creativity, and keep
students excited about school.
Voting YES on the override isn’t a new tax, it’s continuing the support we’ve had for years to
maintain educational excellence, a strong community, and property values.
Join me in voting YES!
Andrea Black
VSD parent/ volunteer/ resident since 2002
Tucson, AZ

Join us in voting YES for Prop 423. The Vail Unified School District delivers one of the highest
percentages of A-Rated Schools in Arizona. Since 1993 Vail’s voter-approved override has
supported the exceptional educational experiences that we expect for our children. Our
community’s support of an override every five years makes this possible. A YES vote for Prop
423 means YES to continued reduced class sizes, to art, music, PE, and enrichment classes. We
see first-hand the commitment of teachers and staff as Vail Preservation Society has worked
with many of them. A yes vote for Prop 423 means that children today will continue to receive
the same exceptional educational opportunities that VUSD students have received since
1993. This is very important to us. Together, our yes votes are an investment in educational
experiences that prepare the next generation for life. Prop 423 will not raise property taxes. It
simply keeps the current override that VUSD uses efficiently in place. Your YES vote for Prop
423 positively impacts the education of every VUSD student.
J.J. Lamb
President & CEO, Vail Preservation Society
Vail, AZ
Jeanne Lumia
Secretary, Executive Board, Vail Preservation Society
Vail, AZ

Reauthorizing the Override is not simply a budget decision-it is a decision about the future
of Vail students. The District’s proven record of academic excellence, responsible financial
management, and strong student outcomes shows that override funds are being used wisely
and effectively. Without this support, the programs, teachers, and classroom conditions that

help students succeed would be at risk. Vail students deserve the same outstanding educational
opportunities that have made this District one of the strongest in Arizona, and voting to
continue the Override is a direct investment in their success, and classroom conditions that
make these achievements possible. Since its original passage, the Override has helped support
exceptional student achievement across the District. The District is ranked #1 among Tucson-
area districts in Arizona by Niche.com, reflecting its continued commitment to academic
excellence.
The District continues to demonstrate strong fiscal stewardship. It holds an A+ Standard
& Poor’s financial rating. The district is among the top 5 percent of districts in Arizona. The
District maintains this rating with a “stable outlook,” underscoring its responsible financial
management and continued ability to invest override funds in programs and staffing that
directly support student success. Vote YES on 423.
Stuart Katz
Vail, AZ

As Citizens of Vail for Education, we urge you to vote YES on Proposition 423.
Vail Unified School District consistently ranks among Arizona’s top 10 school districts,
delivering exceptional academic outcomes for our children. However, maintaining this level of
excellence requires adequate funding. Prop 423 reauthorizes Vail’s existing 12.5% Maintenance
and Operations budget override, directly supporting 20% of our teaching staff. Without this
vote, our schools face devastating cuts to competitive teacher pay, instructional programs,
and small class sizes.
What makes Prop 423 a responsible choice is its efficiency. Vail operates at a significantly lower
override rate than other top-performing Pima County districts. For comparison, neighboring
districts like Tanque Verde Unified (Prop 429) and Sahuarita Unified (Prop 428) run full 15%
budget overrides. Vail continues to deliver top-tier education while maintaining a lower tax
burden.
Prop 423 is a continuation, not a new tax. Voting YES protects our teachers, supports quality
education, and preserves strong property values across our community. Please join us in
investing in Vail’s future by supporting Proposition 423.
Sincerely,
Citizens of Vail for Education
Stefanie Stark, Chair
Vail, AZ
Tameika Symonds, Treasurer
Vail, AZ

At Diamond Ventures, we understand that creating a great place to live requires more than
building homes and businesses. It requires strong schools that families can trust and a
community where children have the opportunity to thrive.
Diamond Ventures has long supported Vail schools and partnered with the district because we
recognize the important role it plays in the success of Southeast Tucson. Many families living
in the communities we have helped develop choose Vail because of its exceptional schools.
VUSD is educating children all the while preparing the future employees, business owners,
and community leaders who will shape this region.
As the Rincon Valley area continues to grow, maintaining a robust, high-performing
educational system is critical. Proposition 423 will help VUSD retain quality teachers and
continue providing the programs and opportunities that have made the district one of the best

in Arizona.
Supporting Proposition 423 protects an essential part of what makes Vail a great place to live,
raise a family, and invest in the future. Diamond Ventures encourages voters to vote YES on
Proposition 423.
Chad Kolodisner
Vice President, Diamond Ventures
Tucson, AZ
